title: Real e-mail address in a snapshot
msg: Real e-mail address {m} is stored in this snapshot. Reserved test domains (@example.com, @example.org, .test, .invalid) are the only safe values here.

title: National identification number
msg: A US Social Security number pattern {m} is committed in this snapshot. National identifiers may only be processed where a legal basis exists; a test fixture is not one.

title: UK National Insurance number
msg: A UK National Insurance number {m} is committed in this snapshot. Use QQ123456C, the number HMRC reserves for examples.

title: Bank account number (IBAN)
msg: {m} passes the ISO 13616 check digits, so it is a usable bank account number sitting in version control.

title: Payment card number
msg: {m} passes the Luhn check, so a real card number is stored in this snapshot. Card data in a repository is outside any cardholder data environment.

title: Reachable phone number
msg: Phone number {m} is stored in this snapshot. Ranges reserved for fiction (+1 555 01xx, +44 7700 900xxx) exist for exactly this case.

title: JSON Web Token
msg: A JWT ({m}) is stored in this snapshot. Its payload is base64, not encryption, and it may still be accepted by your API.

title: Live API credential
msg: Credential {m} is stored in this snapshot. A recorded HTTP response keeps the Authorization header that produced it.

title: Session cookie
msg: A session cookie is recorded on this line ({m}). Whoever reads the repository can replay the session it belongs to.

title: Public IP address
msg: {m} is a routable public IP address. The Court of Justice treated a dynamic IP held by an operator as personal data in C-582/14 (Breyer).

title: Date of birth
msg: A date of birth is filled in on this line ({m}). With a name beside it, this snapshot identifies a person directly.

title: Person's name
msg: A name field carries a real-looking value on this line ({m}). Snapshot fixtures should use obviously invented names.

title: Postal address
msg: A postal address field carries a real-looking value on this line ({m}). A street plus a postcode locates a household.

title: Special category data
msg: This line names a special category of data ({m}). Art. 9 forbids processing it unless one of the ten listed exceptions applies, and testing is not among them.

title: Precise geolocation
msg: Coordinates with four or more decimals ({m}) resolve to about eleven metres — a doorway, not a city.
